title: Website or landing page
fits: Pages people read: a business site, landing page, portfolio, docs or blog. No sign-in and no stored user data.
notFor: accounts, sign-in or anything people save (use the web app recipe)
pages that must change per visitor on the server

stack.why: Fast pages with no JavaScript unless a part needs it; hosts for free as static files.

stack.choice: HTML, CSS and TypeScript where needed
stack.why: Nothing to run on a server.

stack.choice: astro check, plus Playwright with axe for browser and accessibility tests
stack.why: Catches broken pages and accessibility problems before anyone sees them.

after.do: Browser and accessibility tests are added by the kit's set-up (the speed and accessibility test files and a Playwright config that starts npm run preview).

host.name: GitHub Pages (free), or any static host
host.deploy: A GitHub Actions workflow builds the site and publishes the dist folder on every push to main. Set up by /starter-kit:launch; not part of the recipe test.

accounts.name: GitHub
accounts.why: Holds the code, runs the checks and hosts the site.

accounts.name: A domain name
accounts.why: A real address instead of the github.io one.

notes: Pages are files in src/pages/ (.astro or .md); the file path is the address. Shared layout goes in src/layouts/, pieces in src/components/.
Astro components run at build time only: code in the --- block never reaches the browser. Anything interactive needs a <script> tag or a framework component with a client: directive.
Put images that should be optimised in src/assets/ and use Astro's <Image />; files in public/ are copied as they are.
If the site lives at a sub-path (github.io/<repo>/), set site and base in astro.config.mjs, or every link and image breaks after deploy.
No secrets: everything in this project ends up public in the built pages. A form that sends email needs a form service or a small server, which makes it a different recipe.
This is Astro 7: check node_modules/astro/CHANGELOG.md before using any config option or API you remember from an older version.
